correctness.rationale: The deterministic score identity follows by counting transitive triples at their winner. Conditioning on one shared orientation gives exactly zero covariance between distinct centered score squares. A binomial fourth-moment calculation yields their variance. Conditioning on a vertex win set splits cycles into an independent fair sub-tournament count and cross-edge binomial count with zero covariance, producing the exact conditional variance. Orthogonal projection gives the optimal 1/n explained-variance fraction. Exhaustive rational orientation enumeration n=3..6 independently confirms every asserted exact identity.

value.rationale: A single participant score is a natural observable in paired-comparison tournaments; cyclic triangles measure global nontransitivity. The exact optimal nonlinear prediction fraction 1/n, strict contrast with zero linear score covariance, all-score conditional variance formula, and local pairwise orthogonal decomposition form a motivated complete finite-sample dependence calculation, not merely a named-table lookup or arbitrary numerical slice. It quantifies sharply the limits of local scores for predicting global cyclic structure.
